Diagnosis.Molecular Markers: ER+ >95%, PR+ ~70%, HER2- (IHC 0; FISH ratio 0.65), Ki-67 ~20%

Ongoing Treatment Information.Planned Duration: 4 cycles of doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide (AC) every 2 weeks followed by 12 cycles of weekly paclitaxel
Ongoing Treatment Information.Possible Side Effects: fatigue, neuropathy, skin and nail changes, myalgias, alopecia, myelosuppression, nausea, cardiotoxicity, secondary leukemias

Additional Comments: The patient is a 67-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of a right breast partial mastectomy in 2014 for a lipoma, which showed no malignancy at that time. She has a family history of breast cancer, with her paternal great aunts and mother having suffered from the disease. She is physically active, engaging in swimming, walking, and horseback riding. Her gynecologic history includes menarche at 12-13 years, use of oral contraceptives from age 16 for irregular periods, three pregnancies with two live births, use of Clomid in her 30s, first pregnancy at age 30, and menopause at age 57 with a history of night sweats and hot flashes. She has no history of hormone replacement therapy. The patient has decided to proceed with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, specifically the AC/T regimen, and will undergo an echocardiogram, chemotherapy teaching, and port placement before starting treatment. She has also expressed interest in using cold caps to mitigate hair loss during chemotherapy.
